annotation.reasoning_summary: The layer maps housing association property footprints/blocks as discrete bounded objects with attributes like corporation and dwelling counts; polygons are isolated rather than a full tessellation, so PlainVectorRegion and ObjectDS fit best.
Point features represent individual archaeological cesspits/find spots with addresses and photos, so this is a set of identifiable objects rather than measurements or events.
Point features mark distinct archaeological find locations/objects in water soils; this is a point object layer, not a measurement or event layer.

Polygon layer of archaeological sites/vindplaatsen: discrete bounded heritage objects, not a reporting-unit tessellation or full-area coverage. Topology hints and the layer meaning support PlainVectorRegion; entity is ObjectDS because each polygon represents a distinct site/object with descriptive attributes.
Polygons are isolated park/area zones for BBQ restrictions, not a tessellation or reporting unit; decisive rule is selected bounded phenomenon areas -> PatchDS.

Polygons are discrete protected conservation areas, not a full tessellation; topology shows isolated polygons with no shared boundaries. The main meaning is bounded heritage zones, so PatchDS fits best.

Point features mark bee observation locations/areas by year and observed species; the layer is about distinct observation objects, not a measurement or event series. Geometry is PointDS from the Point geometry type.
Point features represent beehive locations, but the main mapped phenomenon is the numeric number of colonies/hives (Aantal_volken/Aantal_kasten), so this is a point-based amount layer.

Polygons form a near-partition with strong shared boundaries, so VectorTessellation. The layer maps soil quality/soil-function zones across the area as an exhaustive thematic classification, which fits CoverageDS.
Point layer of individual trees; each feature is a distinct real-world object with species, age, and owner/manager attributes, so ObjectDS.
Point features represent individual trees with species, height, year planted, owner, and manager attributes; this is an object layer, not a measurement or event layer.
Point features represent individual trees with species, height, year planted, owner, and manager attributes; this is a discrete object layer, not measurements or events.
Point features represent individual trees with species, height, year planted, owner, and manager attributes; this is an object layer, not a measurement or amount layer.
Point locations for neighborhood compost sites; each point is a distinct real-world object/facility, not a measurement or event.

Polygons are selected camera zones rather than a full tessellation; low shared boundaries and sparse adjacency support PlainVectorRegion. The layer represents bounded camera areas, so PatchDS fits the selected-area/zone rule.

Point features represent individual trees, but the layer is mainly about actions and scheduling on those trees (kap/snoei/herplant), so the decisive rule is event-like occurrence/management rather than object inventory.
Point features represent individual crowd-monitoring sensors/cameras, so this is a discrete object layer, not a measurement or amount layer.

Polygons are selected cultural-historical exploration areas, not reporting units or full-area coverage; they represent bounded zones/patches. Topology hint suggested PlainVectorRegion, and the layer is best read as patch-like bounded areas with descriptive attributes.
Point features represent individual knotweed occurrences/locations, not measurements or events; the numeric area field is an attribute of each infestation object, so ObjectDS fits best.
Point feature layer of ecopassage problem sites/solutions; each point represents a distinct real-world crossing/knelpunt object, not a measurement or event.

Polygons are isolated wind-energy potential sites, not a tessellated coverage; the decisive entity rule is object-like bounded projects with numeric attributes (capacity and expected yield), so ObjectDS.
Point layer of polling/stem locations for the 2019 European Parliament election; each point is a distinct voting location with vote attributes, so ObjectDS rather than AmountDS.
Point features mark individual trees/nests (Boom_ID) for oak processionary caterpillar management; this is a discrete object layer with point geometry, not a measurement or event layer.

Polygon areas are selective regulation zones for pedicab rules, not a full tessellation or reporting unit. The decisive rule is bounded selected-area/zone -> PatchDS, with suggested_region_geometry also supporting PlainVectorRegion.
Point features labeled as pedicab/coach pitches; these are distinct real-world standplaatsen (facility/asset objects), not measurements or events.

Point features are individual non-residential premises/addresses (VOT_ID, Adres, Hoofdfunctie), so this is an object layer. The numeric fields are attributes of the premises, not the main mapped phenomenon.
The layer is a categorical land-use/function-mix map with polygons classified as wonen/voorzieningen/werken; it is not a reporting-unit tessellation but a thematic coverage of discrete regions.
Neighborhood (wijken/buurtcombinaties) polygons form a complete administrative partition, and the codes/names indicate reporting units; tessellation + lattice.
Neighborhood-combination polygons are administrative/statistical reporting units that partition Amsterdam, and topology hints strongly support a tessellation; Opp_m2 is just an attribute.
Neighborhood polygons with codes form a near-complete partition of Amsterdam, and the layer is a reporting/statistical unit set (buurten) with area attributes, so VectorTessellation + LatticeDS.
Neighborhoods are reporting/statistical units with codes and area attributes, and the polygons form a near-complete partition with strong shared boundaries, so this is a tessellation plus lattice.

City districts form a near-complete administrative partition, and the topology hints strongly support tessellation. The decisive entity rule is reporting/administrative units, so this is LatticeDS rather than AmountDS despite the area field.

City districts are administrative reporting units that partition Amsterdam, so the geometry is a tessellation. The decisive entity rule is reporting/statistical unit -> LatticeDS; Opp_m2 is just an attribute of each district.

The layer is a complete administrative/area division of Amsterdam into 22 areas plus one extra area feature, with strongly adjacent polygons and high shared boundaries, so it is a tessellation. The features are reporting/administrative units named by gebied and stadsdeel codes, making LatticeDS the best fit.

The layer is a near-complete partition of Amsterdam into 22 areas with shared boundaries and no overlap, so it fits VectorTessellation. The features are reporting/administrative areas with codes and names, so the decisive entity rule is LatticeDS.

The 25 practice areas are named administrative/practice regions that partition Amsterdam, and the topology strongly supports tessellation. The polygons are reporting/aggregation units with area attributes, so LatticeDS is the best fit.

The layer is a near-complete set of named practice areas that partition the city; topology hints strongly support tessellation. The areas function as reporting/administrative units with names, codes, and area fields, so LatticeDS fits best.

The layer is noise contour zones (50 dB, industrial noise), so the main phenomenon is isoline/interval bands rather than objects or reporting units. Polygon features are named contour areas, not a full tessellation, so PlainVectorRegion and ContourDS fit best.

Polygon noise zones are isoline/interval bands (55-60 dB, 60-65 dB, etc.), so the entity is ContourDS. Despite adjacency, the polygons are contour classes rather than a reporting tessellation, so geometry is PlainVectorRegion.
Layer shows noise contour polygons with dB classes; the main phenomenon is isoline/interval bands rather than a full-area tessellation. Classified as ContourDS.

The layer is a set of noise contour polygons with dB classes, so the main phenomenon is contour/isoline bands rather than reporting units or full coverage. Despite strong polygon adjacency, the metadata and classes indicate contour zones, so PlainVectorRegion + ContourDS.
Point features are voting stations/polling locations (stembureaus) with election result attributes, so this is a point object layer rather than a measurement or event layer.

Point layer of identifiable green-roof locations at addresses; the points represent discrete real-world objects/projects, not measurements or events. Numeric fields are attributes, so ObjectDS is the right entity.

Land use 2017 is a full-area thematic classification with many adjacent polygons forming a near-complete partition, so VectorTessellation fits; the polygons represent land-use categories rather than reporting units or individual objects, so CoverageDS.
Point features marking identifiable historical buildings/structures; the main phenomenon is discrete objects, not measurements or events.

The layer shows three discrete municipal polygons with only a GEMEENTE_ID identifier. They are not a full tessellation of a study area; the metadata indicates a special comparison map ('How big is Amsterdam') rather than reporting units or coverage, so PlainVectorRegion. The polygons represent identifiable bounded municipal objects, so ObjectDS.

Polygons mark selected dog run/ban restriction areas rather than a full-area tessellation, so PlainVectorRegion; the main phenomenon is bounded restriction zones/patches, not reporting units, coverage, or objects.

Polygons are discrete green-area objects/selected zones (e.g., parks, cemeteries, corridors) rather than a full administrative or thematic partition, so PlainVectorRegion. The main meaning is bounded green patches/object areas, not reporting units or coverage, so PatchDS.
Point features represent individual elm trees (private); this is a discrete object layer, not a measurement or event layer.
Point features mark distinct housing projects/buildings; the numeric woning count is an attribute, not the main mapped phenomenon, so this is ObjectDS rather than AmountDS.
Point layer of chestnut trees; each point represents a distinct tree object, with species and damage status as attributes. The decisive rule is object points, not amount or event.
Point features sample a continuous climate/hydrology phenomenon (dryness/groundwater metrics like Maaiveld and GLG), so this is PointMeasuresDS; geometry is PointDS.

Polygon layer forms a near-partition with strong shared boundaries, so VectorTessellation. The flooded-area polygons are classified by probability and depth bands, making them contour-like interval zones rather than objects or reporting units.

Point features represent individual market locations (named places like Albert Cuypmarkt and Waterlooplein), so this is an ObjectDS point layer; the metadata indicates markets rather than measurements or events.
Point layer of named green monuments/parks and related sites; the decisive rule is discrete real-world objects at point locations, not amounts or events.
Point features represent individual monumental trees, a set of identifiable real-world objects; numeric and categorical fields are attributes, not the main mapped phenomenon.
Point features represent discrete monument objects/buildings, not measurements or events; the decisive rule is ObjectDS for identifiable real-world assets.

Point features mark individual quay-wall plant occurrences/species locations; the main phenomenon is identifiable objects (plants), not counts. Numeric Aantal_* fields are attributes of those records, so ObjectDS.

MultiPolygon zones are discrete measurement areas rather than a tessellation, and the layer represents NO2 measurements over time at mapped locations/areas. The decisive rule is point/area-based environmental measurement, not object or amount mapping.
Point layer of NO2 measurement locations; each point is a sampling/measurement site for a continuous air-quality phenomenon, so PointDS + PointMeasuresDS.

Polygons are sparse and not a tessellation (low shared boundary, low fill), so PlainVectorRegion. The layer uses category values to classify bounded areas, indicating a full-area thematic coverage rather than reporting units or objects.
Point layer of soundings/boreholes; each point is a measurement location sampling subsurface conditions, so PointDS with PointMeasuresDS.

The layer represents named development neighbourhoods (discrete bounded places) rather than a full administrative/statistical partition, so PlainVectorRegion fits. Each polygon is an identifiable area/project object with codes, names, and links, so ObjectDS is the best entity.
Point layer of discrete public toilet locations; the main phenomenon is identifiable facilities, not the numeric fee attribute, so this is ObjectDS.

Polygon neighborhoods form a tessellation-like partition (high shared boundaries and adjacency). The layer marks selected policy zones with conditions, not reporting units or full coverage, so PatchDS fits best.
Polygon layer with high shared boundaries and adjacent polygons suggests a tessellation. The category field (A/B/C) indicates a full-area parking standard classification, so CoverageDS fits best.

The layer maps named parks/green spaces as discrete bounded objects, not a full-area tessellation; polygons are isolated and the topology hint suggests PlainVectorRegion. Numeric area is only an attribute, so ObjectDS fits best.

Postcode4-buurten are postcode/statistical areas that partition the city, and the strong shared-boundary topology supports VectorTessellation. The decisive entity rule is reporting/statistical units -> LatticeDS; Opp_m2 is just an attribute.
Postcode4-buurten are postcode reporting units that partition the area, and topology hints strongly support tessellation; the decisive entity rule is reporting/statistical units -> LatticeDS.

Postcode6-vlakken are postcode area polygons intended as a partition of the city; the decisive rule is tessellation. They are reporting/statistical units (postcode6 areas) rather than objects or patches, so LatticeDS.
LineString infrastructure layer of roads/transport routes with plus/main network classifications; decisive rule is network system, so Geometry=LineDS and Entity=NetworkDS.
Layer represents pedestrian plus-networks/route areas, so the decisive entity rule is network. Polygons are isolated corridor/zone features rather than a partition, matching PlainVectorRegion.
Points with location names for specific masts/locations; this is a discrete object layer, not measurements or events.
Point features mark distinct privacy-related research/analysis items (e.g., investigations and pilots), so this is a point object layer rather than measurements or events.
Point features mark distinct car-fleet scan locations with names and addresses; this is a set of identifiable objects/measurement sites, not a continuous measurement layer or amount map.

Point features represent polling/stem locations as distinct places in the election layer, not sampled measurements or events. Numeric vote totals are attributes of those locations, so the decisive rule is point-object mapping -> ObjectDS.

Polygons mark selected drainage-possible areas, not a full administrative tessellation; the layer is a bounded phenomenon patch. The categorical Drainage field indicates presence/absence of drainage possibility rather than objects or reporting units.

Polygons are isolated hydro unit areas rather than a partition, so PlainVectorRegion. The layer represents selected Rainproof hydro units/solution areas, not reporting units, coverage, or objects; PatchDS fits bounded phenomenon zones.

Polygons mark selected rainproof bottleneck areas, not a reporting-unit tessellation; topology also shows isolated polygons, so PlainVectorRegion. The layer is about bounded problem zones/affected areas, fitting PatchDS.

Polygons are 19 isolated location areas for Rainproof polder sewerage sites, not a reporting-unit tessellation; the layer is best read as selected bounded project zones/patches rather than coverage or objects.
Point features mark distinct religious buildings/places with names, addresses, and denominations, so this is an object layer rather than an amount or event layer.
Line geometry and the layer maps sidewalk segments with width/spaceclaim attributes. This is a linear infrastructure/object layer, not a network route system or numeric amount layer.
Line features depict a connected roadway/traffic route system for mopeds on streets, so the decisive rule is network infrastructure rather than object or amount.
Point features with names, sport type, location, and photos indicate discrete public sports facilities; the main phenomenon is identifiable objects, not measurements or events.
Point locations for city farming sites (gardens, farms, cooperatives) are discrete real-world places, so this is an ObjectDS layer with PointDS geometry.

The layer maps discrete city farming sites/terrain parcels with names, addresses, and websites, so they are identifiable objects rather than a tessellation or coverage. The polygons are isolated and do not form a partition, supporting PlainVectorRegion.

Point features represent discrete initiatives/locations ('Stadsloods' city pilot projects) with initiative name, activity, sector, and year; this is a point object layer, not a measurement or event layer.
Major streets are a connected street/route system, and the layer consists of LineString features. The decisive rule is network infrastructure on lines, not the numeric line numbers.
LineString features named district heating/cooling transport indicate a connected utility transport network; STATUS/NETTYPE are attributes of the network, not the main phenomenon.

Polygon areas for district heating/cooling zones by neighbourhood are selected service areas, not a reporting-unit tessellation; topology is sparse and the layer is best treated as bounded phenomenon patches.

Polygons are discrete project/strategy areas for housing plans, not a full administrative tessellation; the decisive rule is bounded selected zones/patches. Numeric dwelling maxima are attributes, not the main mapped phenomenon.
Point layer of named local farming products businesses/facilities with addresses and categories; the points represent identifiable objects, not measurements or events.
LineString features represent tram and metro route infrastructure; this is a connected transport network, not a set of independent line objects or amounts.
Title and properties indicate tram and metro lines; this is a connected transport route system, so the decisive rule is network. Geometry is LineDS because all features are LineString.
Point geometry and the layer represents tram stops and metro stations, which are discrete real-world transport facilities; numeric radius is just an attribute, not the main phenomenon.
Point layer of named tram stops and metro stations; features are discrete transport facilities/routes stops, so PointDS with ObjectDS (not AmountDS because numeric fields are just attributes).

Point features represent individual traffic-light-controlled intersections/locations, with identifiers, names, status, and metadata about each object; this is a point object layer, not an amount or event layer.

Line geometries represent traffic links/roads, and the mapped phenomenon is traffic volume/prognosis values on those links (etmaal and time-period counts), so this is a network-like line layer with AmountDS as the main meaning.

Point layer of election polling/stem locations; each point represents a voting location object with vote statistics, so geometry is PointDS and entity is ObjectDS (polling-station objects, not an AmountDS layer).
Point features represent individual replacement trees identified by species, ID, planting year, and size classes; this is an object layer, not an amount or event layer.

Point features represent identifiable traffic information system devices (e.g., cameras, displays, triggers) with object IDs and locations, so this is PointDS and ObjectDS rather than an amount or event layer.
Point features represent distinct traffic information system installations (BFA units) with IDs, types, and locations; this is an object layer, not measurements or events.
Point map of breeding bird locations; the main phenomenon is bird count/abundance by site and year, so this is a point AmountDS rather than just objects.
Point features represent individual park benches (distinct physical objects) in Vondelpark; the numeric/text fields are attributes, not the main phenomenon.

Line features represent street segments (straatvakken) and the layer maps walkability/pressure ratings along those segments; this is a line-based thematic amount/classification layer rather than a network of routes or discrete objects.
Point geometry; each feature is a distinct wall-art artwork at a specific building/address, so the main phenomenon is identifiable objects rather than amounts or events.
Polygons have strong tessellation topology and the layer maps welstand/quality categories ('Niveau') across the area as an exhaustive thematic coverage, so CoverageDS with VectorTessellation.

The polygons form a near-complete tessellation (high shared boundaries, many adjacencies) and the layer is a categorical area-wide classification of building/urban ‘welstand’ systems, so CoverageDS fits better than object or patch.
Point locations mark WWII attack/incidents at addresses; the main phenomenon is events that occurred at specific places, not objects or measurements.

The layer shows discrete housing plan project polygons, not a full-area partition; topology also suggests isolated/selected regions, so PlainVectorRegion. The features primarily represent identifiable project areas with housing-plan attributes and phase/status fields, so ObjectDS rather than AmountDS.
Point locations represent identifiable self-build plot projects/plots with names, contacts, and status attributes, so this is a point object layer rather than amount or event.

The layer is a polygon thematic classification about solar-panels/heritage categories, not a reporting-unit tessellation. The categories indicate an area-wide classification of regions, so CoverageDS; the topology hint suggests isolated/partial polygons rather than a full partition, so PlainVectorRegion.
Point features represent solar panel locations/objects; numeric fields are attributes (panel count and capacity), not the main phenomenon, so this is ObjectDS rather than AmountDS.
Point features with names and categories represent distinct swimming locations/facilities, so this is a point object layer (not amounts or events).
